column4: MAKI02 16-colour patch at (194,125)-(262,146). The encoder drops the last flag-A bit, so the last colour read runs 2 bytes past EOF and RECOIL rejects it. With 2 zero bytes appended, RECOIL's output is identical to ours. Forcing that bit consumes flag B and the colour stream exactly and gives the same pixels, so the result is unambiguous. Render shows a coherent eye-and-glasses crop.

MAKI02 2x1 patch at (622,332) from the same encoder (last flag-A bit dropped, colour read 2 bytes past EOF), so RECOIL rejects it. With 2 bytes appended, RECOIL matches ours. Either reading of the flag gives 8 pixels of palette colour 0.

Big-endian MAKI02 variant from an X68000 game: no machine name, every header field big-endian. RECOIL reads the header little-endian and rejects it. Flag A, flag B and colour streams are consumed exactly as sized (1 trailing pad byte). Render shows a coherent snowy-night scene.
